I started a new job a few months ago.
I was excited about the fresh start, a new team, and a company I'd been hoping to get into for a solid year before finally landing the offer.
On my first day, HR walked me around for introductions.
About halfway through the tour, we stopped at an office, and the person who stood up to shake my hand was, unmistakably, my ex, hair a little shorter but everything else exactly the same.
We'd dated for almost two years, back before either of us had "real" jobs.
We hadn't spoken since a breakup that, while not dramatic, had been awkward enough that we never really stayed in touch.
We'd been perfectly polite about the whole thing back then too, one of those quiet, mutual endings.
There was no real fighting, just two people slowly drifting into completely different directions after graduation.
For a solid second, neither of us said anything.
We just sort of stood there processing the situation, while HR cheerfully explained that this person would actually be my direct manager going forward.
We both recovered fast enough to shake hands like completely normal professionals.
Though I'm fairly sure my smile looked slightly more like a grimace for at least the first thirty seconds, my hand noticeably slower to let go than it should have been.
The first week was, honestly, a little tense.
Both of us were extremely polite in this overly formal way that neither of us had ever used with each other back when we actually dated.
We both called each other by our full names in meetings, way more formally than either of us called anyone else on the team.
Honestly, that probably made things look weirder than if we'd just acted normal.
By week two, though, we'd more or less settled into it.
We even started joking quietly about the sheer absurdity of the situation, like the time we accidentally both used an old inside joke in a meeting.
A coworker eventually found out we used to date, and word apparently spread through the office fast.
Thankfully, everyone mostly just found it funny instead of making the whole thing unnecessarily weird, occasionally asking us for old college photos as proof.
A year later, it's honestly just normal now.
My ex is a genuinely good manager, and the story has become the go-to icebreaker whenever someone new joins the team.

New hires usually don't believe it at first, assuming it's some kind of office urban legend, until my ex casually confirms it herself during their very first meeting, completely deadpan, like it's the most normal thing in the world.
